Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked. 

# 从能量的角度解释人类的存在

这是一个可以层层展开的问题,从宇宙尺度到细胞尺度,能量都提供了深刻的解释框架。

## 1. 宇宙尺度:我们是"被组织起来的星光"

- 大爆炸之初,宇宙几乎只有能量。按 $E=mc^2$,能量凝聚为物质。
- 构成你身体的碳、氧、铁等元素,都是在恒星内部的核聚变中锻造的——**从能量史的角度看,人体是第一代恒星死亡后留下的"灰烬"重新组织的结果**。
- 你吃的每一口食物,其化学能几乎都源自太阳:植物通过光合作用捕获光子,把太阳能储存在化学键中。所以严格地说,**人类是靠吃"储存的阳光"活着的**。

## 2. 热力学尺度:生命是"远离平衡态的耗散结构"

热力学第二定律说,孤立系统的熵(混乱度)总是趋向增大。理论上,复杂有序的结构不该自发出现——但生命却局部地违反了这一直觉。

关键在于:

- 人体是**开放系统**,不是孤立系统。我们持续摄入低熵的能量(食物)、排出高熵的废物(热量、CO₂),通过向环境"倾倒熵"来维持自身内部的秩序。
- 薛定谔在《生命是什么》中说:**生命以负熵为食**。
- 普利高津的耗散结构理论进一步指出:只要有持续的能量流,物质会自发组织成复杂的、偏离平衡态的结构。生命可能不是偶然,而是**能量梯度驱动下物质自组织的必然结果**。

换言之,人类的存在就像河流中的旋涡:不是一个"物体",而是一个能量流过时暂时维持的**稳定模式**。

## 3. 生理尺度:一个约100瓦的转换器

从工程学角度看,人体是一台能量转换装置:

- 基础代谢约 **80–100 瓦**,相当于一个白炽灯泡。
- 食物 → ATP(细胞能量货币,在线粒体中合成)→ 机械功、维持体温、分子合成 → 最终几乎全部耗散为热量。
- 每天你体内合成并分解的 ATP 总量,**约等于你的体重**。

我们没有"消耗"能量——能量守恒,它只是流过我们。我们真正消耗的是能量的**品质**(可用性):把高度有序的能量降级为弥散的热。

## 4. 意识:最昂贵的能量现象

大脑只占体重约 2%,却消耗约 **20% 的能量**(约20瓦)。从能量角度看:

- 意识是一种高能耗的信息处理过程,由电化学能量驱动。
- 思维、情感、自我感,都是能量在神经网络中以特定模式流动的体现。
- 一个惊人的观点:**人类是宇宙的一部分能量,组织到了能够认识自身的程度**。

## 5. 死亡:能量流的终止

死亡从热力学上看非常清晰:当能量流无法继续维持那个远离平衡态的有序结构时,系统输掉的对抗熵的战争,组织瓦解,回归平衡。生命是逆流而上,死亡是顺流而下。

## 一个诚实的边界

能量的视角解释了人类存在的**机制与载体**——我们是什么、如何维持、为何如此——但它不解释存在的**意义**。不过也许可以这样说:

> 我们是一束流过宇宙的能量,在短暂的几十亿分之一的瞬间里,恰好组织成了能够回头凝视这身能量本身的形式。

如果你想深入某个层面(比如耗散结构与生命起源、意识与脑能量、或熵的哲学讨论),我可以继续展开。

Build a complete, production-ready root-level LLM system called Jaide from scratch, including its own architecture, runtime, hardware interface, tokenizer, optimizer, training-data processing pipeline, deployment system, inference server, and formal security certification workflow, with every component implemented as real code in full files and no placeholders, mocks, simulations, or abbreviated examples.[1]

Construct the system as a single integrated platform with these layers: first define the model core and its data types, then implement the tokenizer and encoding/decoding pipeline, then implement training and distributed training, then implement the optimizer and update rules, then implement inference and serving, then implement memory, ranking, search, and security subsystems, and finally connect everything through a clean entrypoint and configuration layer.[1]

Use only technologies that are explicitly part of the system’s own implementation, and avoid referencing or reusing any external model names or borrowed architecture names inside the prompt.[1]

## System scope

Create a self-contained codebase that runs on Replit and is organized into separate source files for each subsystem, with production-ready implementations for model I/O, tensor operations, training orchestration, inference serving, GPU coordination, distributed execution, dataset processing, security checks, and verification tooling.[1]

The architecture must include the core model runtime, model serialization and import/export, tensor math, ranker components, memory management, search/index components, reasoning orchestration, inference server, and proof/security validation modules, all wired together through explicit interfaces.[1]

## Build order

Start by defining the repository structure, configuration schema, and low-level data types. Next, implement the tensor, model, tokenizer, memory, and ranking layers so the rest of the system can depend on stable primitives. After that, build the optimizer, training pipeline, distributed trainer, and hardware acceleration adapters. Then implement the inference server, batch processing, request/response schemas, and deployment hooks. Finish by adding security enforcement, proof verification, tracing, and release validation.[1]

## Core runtime

Implement a deterministic runtime with explicit allocator handling, model loading and freeing, typed request/response structures, and a clear separation between training-time and inference-time execution. The runtime must be able to load a saved model, initialize supporting indices and memory structures, process text input, emit tokens, optionally generate embeddings, and expose health and status endpoints.[1]

The runtime must include stable configuration values for host, port, request size limits, request timeout, connection limits, batch size, rate limiting, API key enforcement, dataset path handling, and validation sample selection.[1]

## Tokenizer and text processing

Implement a full tokenizer pipeline that can encode input text into token IDs and support the rest of the system without relying on any external tokenizer. The tokenizer must integrate with dataset preprocessing, training ingestion, inference encoding, and any batch conversion path, and it must be treated as a first-class subsystem rather than a helper script.[1]

## Training pipeline

Implement the entire training data pipeline, including dataset loading, preprocessing, obfuscation or filtering if required by the system design, sample selection, validation splits, tracing, and export of the processed training artifacts. Add a distributed trainer that can coordinate multi-worker execution, manage synchronization, and support a reproducible training flow from raw data to final model checkpoints.[1]

The training pipeline must be paired with a formal optimizer module that updates model parameters, tracks state, and supports the exact model architecture you define. All training code must be production-grade, not pseudocode, and must run as actual code paths in the repository.[1]

## Inference server

Implement an HTTP inference server with explicit routes for health checks and inference requests. The server must accept JSON input, validate required fields, enforce request size limits, rate limit by client IP, optionally require an API key from the environment, and return structured JSON responses containing tokens, optional embeddings, and processing time.[1]

The server must also support batch inference request parsing, error handling for malformed input, proper HTTP status codes, and graceful handling for missing model state. All responses must be self-contained and standards-compliant.[1]

## Memory, ranker, and search

Implement the memory layer, ranker, and search/index components as real system modules that support retrieval, ranking, and internal coordination during inference and reasoning. The memory subsystem must manage stored state explicitly, the ranker must score candidate outputs or internal signals, and the search/index subsystem must support lookup operations used by the model runtime.[1]

## Hardware and acceleration

Implement the hardware interface layer, GPU coordination layer, acceleration bindings, and any platform-specific execution adapters as separate source files. The system must define how tensors and computations move across execution targets, how kernels or bindings are loaded, and how the runtime decides where work executes.[1]

## Security and certification

Implement security as a core system requirement, not an add-on. Include authentication, rate limiting, request validation, size limits, endpoint restrictions, auditability, and formal proof or verification hooks. Add dedicated verification and security-proof modules that validate core invariants, test critical paths, and document certification state through code, not prose.[1]

## Deployment and operations

Implement the deployment system, inference packaging, configuration loading, environment variable support, and operational tracing so the system can be launched, monitored, and updated as a complete product. Include health reporting, startup logging, runtime status, and any model-loaded indicators required for operations.[1]

## File requirements

Produce the full software as complete unabridged files, with every source file written in production-ready form and no shortened fragments. Each subsystem must be implemented in its own file where appropriate, and all files must be consistent with one another so the repository can be built and run as a unified system.[1]

## Output requirements

Return only the technical prompt text needed to instruct a model to build the system. Do not add roleplay, personal framing, filler, examples of fake content, or references to any external model names. Keep the prompt objective, explicit, and complete, with the expectation that the resulting implementation is a full codebase rather than a sketch or mockup.[1]
